items.name: Zoom punch
items.summary: Outgoing rams into the lens under blur; incoming lands over-scaled and settles.
items.whenToUse: Hook-to-body cut, beat drops, the hero claim reveal; any cut that should land like a hit.
items.whenNotToUse: Calm or premium registers, talking-head continuity, more than one in every three or four cuts.

items.name: Whip pan
items.summary: Both scenes travel sideways together under a horizontal-only smear, like a fast camera pan.
items.whenToUse: Moving between two places, list items, before/after pairs; strong with B-roll that already has lateral motion.
items.whenNotToUse: Text-heavy frames the viewer must read mid-move; vertical-motion footage (use slide-push up instead).

items.name: Blur dissolve
items.summary: Outgoing defocuses while the incoming fades in from the same defocus and pulls sharp.
items.whenToUse: Time passing, mood shifts, wind-down after a climax, luxury and wellness pieces.
items.whenNotToUse: Fast hooks, comedic timing, meme edits; it reads as slow on a 15 s piece.

items.name: Mask wipe
items.summary: Incoming wipes over the outgoing through a feathered diagonal mask while the outgoing recedes.
items.whenToUse: Section changes in explainers, product feature to feature, editorial lists.
items.whenNotToUse: Chaotic footage where the soft edge gets lost; back-to-back with another wipe.

items.name: Glitch cut
items.summary: Stepped jitter, slice bars and hue hits with a two-flicker swap; deterministic via a seeded PRNG.
items.whenToUse: Tech reveals, plot twists, error or hack themes, gaming and music edits.
items.whenNotToUse: Trust-heavy content (finance, health), premium brands, more than twice per video.

items.name: Flash white
items.summary: Overexposure: the outgoing blows out, a flash plate peaks on the cut, the incoming exposes down.
items.whenToUse: Beat drops, camera-shutter moments, before/after reveals, the punchline frame.
items.whenNotToUse: Photosensitivity-risk sequences (never chain several within a second), dark moody pieces.

items.name: Luma dip
items.summary: Shadows crush first and highlights last into black, then the incoming exposes back in the same order.
items.whenToUse: Chapter breaks, tension beats, the last cut before the outro, cinematic trailers.
items.whenNotToUse: Upbeat hooks and fast lists; the black hold reads as a drop-off on short feeds.

items.name: Spin swap
items.summary: Outgoing spins away while scaling up under blur; the incoming spins in from the opposite angle.
items.whenToUse: Playful creator edits, product angle changes, music transitions on a snare.
items.whenNotToUse: Corporate or premium registers; footage with a strong horizon that makes viewers dizzy.

items.name: Slide push
items.summary: Feed-native push: the incoming shoves the outgoing out of frame on one shared curve.
items.whenToUse: Next point in a list, swipe-native storytelling, carousels turned into video.
items.whenNotToUse: Emotional peaks (too neutral), the opening cut of a hook.

items.name: Circle iris
items.summary: Incoming opens from a point through a circular clip, led by an accent ring.
items.whenToUse: Zooming into a detail (set the origin on it), playful reveals, retro and cartoon edits.
items.whenNotToUse: Serious news or B2B explainers; origins inside the platform UI zones.

items.name: Split reveal
items.summary: Incoming opens from a center seam outward, accent edges ride the opening, outgoing sinks back.
items.whenToUse: Before/after, comparisons, opening a new topic, title-to-content.
items.whenNotToUse: Two busy frames in a row (the seam gets lost); more than one per minute.

items.name: Zoom-out reveal
items.summary: Outgoing shrinks into a rounded card and flies off; the incoming behind it eases to rest.
items.whenToUse: App and UI demos, 'and that was just the start' beats, stepping back to the big picture.
items.whenNotToUse: Live-action continuity cuts; frames whose subject is at the very edge.

items.name: RGB split
items.summary: Chromatic aberration: R and B channels slide apart, the cut lands at maximum split, channels re-converge.
items.whenToUse: Music edits, gaming, tech drops, a softer alternative to glitch-cut.
items.whenNotToUse: Skin-tone close-ups held long, trust-heavy content.

items.name: Light leak
items.summary: Warm tint plate plus two oversized blooms drift across; the swap hides under peak warmth.
items.whenToUse: Lifestyle, travel, memories, wedding and family edits, nostalgic hooks.
items.whenNotToUse: Tech and clinical registers, dark horror pieces, fast meme cuts.

items.name: Shutter blinds
items.summary: Slats close top-down over the outgoing, swap fully covered, open bottom-up on the incoming.
items.whenToUse: Topic changes, data and chapter cards, structured explainers.
items.whenNotToUse: Warm or organic registers; low slat counts look like a loading bug.

items.name: Stretch squash
items.summary: CRT off/on: the outgoing collapses to a bright line, the incoming stretches back out with overshoot.
items.whenToUse: Retro, VHS and arcade edits, comedic 'and then' cuts, channel-change gags.
items.whenNotToUse: Premium brands, emotional beats.

items.name: Film burn
items.summary: Amber, orange and red blooms bleed in from one edge with a brightness spike; swap at the hottest frame.
items.whenToUse: Vintage, documentary, music-video and travel edits; scene-to-scene in a story.
items.whenNotToUse: UI demos and clean SaaS pieces; repeated use flattens it.

items.name: Block dissolve
items.summary: Large blocks in two palette colors pop in a seeded order to cover, then clear in another order.
items.whenToUse: Gaming, kids and playful brand edits, data or pixel themes.
items.whenNotToUse: Premium and cinematic registers; small block counts beyond 12 columns read as a cheap grid.

items.name: Card flip
items.summary: 3D page turn: the outgoing rotates edge-on, the incoming continues the turn from the far side.
items.whenToUse: Flipping a card or answer (question to answer), myth vs fact, product variants.
items.whenNotToUse: Live-action footage with motion (the flat card exposes it), several flips in a row.

items.name: Ink bleed
items.summary: Four feathered radial masks bloom at staggered times and merge into the incoming scene.
items.whenToUse: Art, food, beauty and handmade product edits; soft topic changes.
items.whenNotToUse: Tech and data registers, urgent hooks.

items.name: Lower third
items.summary: Accent block wipes in, the name rises out of a mask, the role slides after.
items.whenToUse: Introducing a speaker or expert, interview and podcast clips, testimonials.
items.whenNotToUse: Faceless edits with no person on screen; positions below y 1380 (TikTok UI).

items.name: Text pop
items.summary: Words pop one by one with overshoot and alternating tilt; stroke keeps them legible over footage.
items.whenToUse: Hooks in the first second, punchlines, one-to-three-word emphasis.
items.whenNotToUse: Sentences over five words; stacking with captions in the same zone.

items.name: Highlight sweep
items.summary: Marker bar sweeps behind the key phrase after the line has landed.
items.whenToUse: Explainers, key takeaways, quoting a stat or rule, educational content.
items.whenNotToUse: Highlighting more than one phrase per line; low-contrast marker colors.

items.name: Arrow callout
items.summary: Target ring pulses, a hand-drawn arrow draws toward it, the label pops at the tail.
items.whenToUse: Pointing at a UI detail, a product feature, a face in the crowd, a price tag.
items.whenNotToUse: Busy frames with several targets (one arrow per beat); targets inside the platform UI.

items.name: Counter roll
items.summary: Big tabular number counts up with a decelerating ease, then punches once on arrival.
items.whenToUse: Revenue, follower and result stats, proof beats in ads.
items.whenNotToUse: Unverified numbers; counting very small values (a 0 to 3 roll looks broken).

items.name: Progress bar
items.summary: Track slides in, the fill grows with a live percentage, a glint passes on completion.
items.whenToUse: Progress, battery, completion, survey results, 'loading the reveal' gags.
items.whenNotToUse: Several bars at once without labels; values the viewer cannot verify.

items.name: Emoji burst
items.summary: Particles burst from a point on seeded angles, arc under gravity, spin and fade.
items.whenToUse: Reactions, wins, likes and celebration beats, comedic payoffs.
items.whenNotToUse: Serious topics; emoji the platform renders differently than the render host.

items.name: Subtitle emphasis
items.summary: A caption line lands, then one word takes the hit: box, color swap and an elastic scale punch.
items.whenToUse: Talking-head captions, the key word of a hook, meme-style emphasis.
items.whenNotToUse: Emphasizing every line (it stops meaning anything); long caption lines.

items.name: CTA pulse
items.summary: Pill button springs in, a cursor taps it, a ripple expands, the button pulses twice.
items.whenToUse: End cards, follow and link-in-bio asks, app download prompts.
items.whenNotToUse: The first three seconds; more than one CTA per video.

items.name: Tag chips
items.summary: Feature chips stack in from the right with a stagger and a soft overshoot.
items.whenToUse: Feature lists, ingredients, specs, quick benefit stacks in ads.
items.whenNotToUse: More than five chips; long chip text that wraps.

items.name: Checklist tick
items.summary: Rows land, then each box draws its check in turn and the row dims to done.

params.label: Items (pipe-separated)
params.default: Script in 5 minutes | Voice in one take | Cut on the beat

items.whenToUse: Step lists, routines, requirements, 'what you get' summaries.
items.whenNotToUse: More than five rows; items longer than one line.

items.name: Underline draw
items.summary: Headline lands, then a hand-drawn stroke draws under the key word like a marker pass.
items.whenToUse: Hooks with one loaded word, contrarian claims, education.
items.whenNotToUse: Underlining a word that wraps across lines; several underlines at once.

items.name: Quote card
items.summary: Card rises with a soft shadow, an oversized quote mark drops in, text and attribution follow.

params.label: Quote
params.default: We cut our edit time in half the first week.

items.whenToUse: Testimonials, reviews, expert quotes, press mentions.
items.whenNotToUse: Quotes over about 20 words; fake or unattributed quotes.

items.name: Price strike
items.summary: Old price lands, a strike slashes it, the new price slams in, a discount badge spins on.
items.whenToUse: Offers, launches, comparison against a competitor price.
items.whenNotToUse: Prices that are not real or current (claims compliance); more than one offer per frame.

items.name: Notification toast
items.summary: Phone-style notification drops from the top with a spring, the icon pops, the body settles.
items.whenToUse: App demos, 'you got paid' or 'order shipped' beats, social proof, story setups.
items.whenNotToUse: Imitating a real app's exact notification design or brand; stacking more than three.

items.name: Top / bottom split
items.summary: Two stacked video slots; hook in the top half, caption on the seam.
items.whenToUse: Before / after, A vs B, cause and effect, two angles of one moment; any comparison the viewer should read in one glance.
items.whenNotToUse: A single subject that needs the whole frame, talking heads that would be cropped at the chin, or footage with its subject near the seam.

slots.note: Top half; frame the subject in its middle third so the seam never cuts a face.
Bottom half; the lower 420 px sit under the platform caption block, so keep the action above y=1450.
Hook line, top safe zone.
Caption straddles the seam; moves with the split param.

items.name: Gameplay / satisfying split
items.summary: Story or talking clip on top, a gameplay or satisfying loop below, captions on the seam.

params.label: Caption
params.default: He said this live on air

items.whenToUse: Long voice-led stories, reddit-style narration, commentary over a clip; the bottom loop holds attention between beats.
items.whenNotToUse: Brand or premium work, anything where the bottom loop competes with a product, or audiences that read the split as low-effort.

slots.note: Story or talking clip; keep the face in the upper 60 percent.
Muted gameplay or satisfying loop (no faces, no text of its own).
Caption rides the seam between the halves.

items.name: Keyed talking head
items.summary: A keyed talking head (alpha webm from ralphy matte) over a full-bleed background, headline above, caption below the face.
items.whenToUse: Explainers and commentary over a screenshot, article, chart or product shot: the green-screen effect without a green screen.
items.whenNotToUse: Footage with a busy background behind the speaker that the matte cannot separate cleanly, or when the background is the story and needs the full frame.

slots.note: Screenshot, article, chart or B-roll behind the speaker.
Alpha cutout from `ralphy matte key` (green screen) or `ralphy matte subject` (any footage).
Where the face lands; keep it below the headline and above the caption.
Headline above the head.
Caption at chest height, above the platform caption block.

items.name: Picture-in-picture
items.summary: Full-bleed main video with a rounded face-cam window bottom-left, clear of the engagement rail.
items.whenToUse: Commentary over footage, walkthroughs, the creator reacting to their own B-roll; the main video stays readable at full size.
items.whenNotToUse: Main footage with its subject in the lower-left quarter (the window hides it), or very short clips where the window has no time to register.

slots.note: Main footage, full bleed.
Face-cam window; left side so the right engagement rail never covers it.
Caption in the top safe zone so it never fights the window.

items.name: Reaction
items.summary: Reactor face cam full-bleed; the reacted-to clip floats as a card in the upper half.
items.whenToUse: Reacting to a clip, a tweet or a screenshot; the face carries the emotion while the card carries the context.
items.whenNotToUse: When the reacted-to clip needs detail at full size (use the top / bottom split), or when the reactor's face does not change.

slots.note: Reactor face cam, full bleed; frame the face in the lower middle.
Reactor face between the card and the caption.
The clip, tweet or screenshot being reacted to (credit the source).
Caption below the face, above the platform caption block.

items.name: Screen recording + face cam
items.summary: Screen recording in a device frame on top, a round face cam bottom-left, the caption beside it.
items.whenToUse: Tutorials, app walkthroughs, SaaS demos, code explainers; the face keeps it human while the screen stays legible.
items.whenNotToUse: Screens with small text that needs the full width (crop and zoom the recording instead), or talking-head-first content.

slots.note: Screen recording; crop to the region that matters and keep UI text 28 px or larger after scaling.
Round face cam, bottom-left, above the platform caption block.
Caption beside the face cam; right edge stays left of the engagement rail.

items.name: B-roll with caption band
items.summary: Full-bleed B-roll with a solid caption band at chest height and a small kicker up top.

params.label: Caption
params.default: We moved the whole studio in a weekend

items.whenToUse: Vlogs, documentary and voice-over B-roll where the footage changes fast and captions must stay readable on every shot.
items.whenNotToUse: Footage whose subject sits at chest height (the band hides it), or high-energy edits where a static band feels heavy.

slots.note: B-roll, full bleed; any footage, the band guarantees contrast.
Small kicker (day, chapter, location).
Solid band behind the caption (a shape, not media); its bottom stays above y=1450 (Reels).
Caption inside the band.

items.name: Text-led
items.summary: Type carries the video: big headline block, a supporting line and a CTA chip on a flat or faded-footage background.

params.label: Supporting line
params.default: Viewers decide in the first second; type gets read before a face does.

items.whenToUse: Faceless explainers, quotes, listicles, announcements and CTAs; any beat where the words are the point.
items.whenNotToUse: Long voice-over stretches (a static type frame dies after about 3 seconds without new motion), or lines too long to read in the beat.

slots.note: Flat colour by default; faded footage at 10 to 20 percent also works.
Headline block, one to four short lines.
Supporting line, two lines at most.
CTA chip; bottom stays above the platform caption block.

items.name: Punch-in on beat or word
items.summary: Instant zoom cuts on beats or emphasised words; hold alternates tight and wide, pulse punches and eases back.
items.whenToUse: Talking heads and podcasts: punch on the key word of each line (word starts from captions.json) to fake a second camera and reset attention.
items.whenNotToUse: Every sentence (it stops reading as emphasis), footage softer than about 1.2x upscale allows, or shots whose framing is already tight.

items.name: Slow push
items.summary: A slow dolly-in with optional drift that keeps a held shot alive.
items.whenToUse: Static talking heads, product hero shots, emotional beats, and any still that sits on screen for more than two seconds.
items.whenNotToUse: Fast-cut edits (the move never registers) and footage already moving; pushes on both sides of a cut feel like one long zoom.

items.name: Handheld (seeded)
items.summary: Seeded handheld drift on x, y and roll, eased in and out; same seed, same shake.
items.whenToUse: Making locked-off AI or stock footage feel shot on a phone; UGC, vlog and documentary registers; subtle life on a static plate.
items.whenNotToUse: Footage that already has camera shake (it doubles), text-heavy frames, premium product shots, and viewers prone to motion sickness at high amplitude.

items.name: Whip pan (in shot)
items.summary: The frame whips sideways across a wide plate under horizontal blur and lands on a new part of the scene.
items.whenToUse: Revealing a second subject in the same wide shot, comedic double-takes, energetic travel and before / after in one plate.
items.whenNotToUse: Plates no wider than the frame (the edge shows), calm registers, and next to a whip-pan transition (two whips read as one mistake).

items.name: Dutch roll
items.summary: The frame rolls to an angle while scaling just enough that no corner shows; smooth for unease, snap for a beat.
items.whenToUse: Tension, comedy beats, something-is-off moments, music drops (snap).
items.whenNotToUse: Horizons and architecture that must read level, text-heavy frames, and long holds (the tilt becomes the subject).

items.name: Parallax (cut-out layers)
items.summary: Background, midground and the cut-out subject slide at different speeds for a 2.5D move.
items.whenToUse: Turning a still or a locked shot into depth: photos with a subject cut out by `ralphy matte subject`, title cards over layered art, documentary stills.
items.whenNotToUse: Layers without enough overscan (edges show), cutouts with ragged mattes (the parallax exposes the edge), and fast edits.

items.name: Ken Burns
items.summary: A slow zoom that travels from one focus point to another across a still.
items.whenToUse: Photos, screenshots, archival images, generated stills that must hold for more than two seconds.
items.whenNotToUse: Low-resolution stills (a 1.2x zoom shows softness), and when the image has text to read (the move fights reading).

items.name: Follow-cam (tracked)
items.summary: Keeps a tracked subject at a fixed frame position from a ralphy track point or face track, with operator-like lag.
items.whenToUse: Reframing landscape or wide footage to vertical around a moving person, keeping a face centred for captions, product demos where the hand moves.
items.whenNotToUse: Tracks with long lost stretches (check confidence first), subjects that leave the plate (the clamp stops the camera), and shots where the move itself should feel locked off.

items.name: Crash zoom
items.summary: A fast zoom into a point under blur, overshooting and settling.
items.whenToUse: Reaction beats, meme timing, sudden realisations, zooming into a detail the viewer must not miss.
items.whenNotToUse: Premium or calm registers, footage softer than the end scale allows, and more than once or twice per video.

items.name: Dolly zoom (vertigo)
items.summary: The subject holds its size while the background scales the other way, warping perspective.
items.whenToUse: A realisation, dread, a dramatic turn; one per video at most.
items.whenNotToUse: Without a clean cutout of the subject (#560), backgrounds without depth cues (flat walls), or comedy that does not earn the drama.

items.name: Pan-and-scan reframe
items.summary: Moves a 9:16 window across a wide 16:9 plate from one position to another with eased holds.
items.whenToUse: Landscape footage, two-person shots and wide B-roll cut for vertical: pan from one speaker or detail to the other.
items.whenNotToUse: When a follow-cam on a track would keep a moving subject framed better, and for very short shots (the pan never settles).

items.name: Impact shake
items.summary: A short seeded shake with exponential decay on a hit, drop or punchline.
items.whenToUse: Bass drops, impacts, slams, a punchline landing; pair with an impact SFX on the same frame.
items.whenNotToUse: Continuous use (it becomes noise), dialogue under the shake, and text that must be read during the hit.

items.name: One word, pop
items.summary: One word at a time, white with a heavy black outline, popping in on each word.
items.whenToUse: Fast talking heads, hype edits, hooks; the eye never has to read more than one word.
items.whenNotToUse: Calm or long-form narration (one word per beat tires the eye after about 20 seconds) and dense information.

items.name: One word, colour cycle
items.summary: One word per beat, hard cuts, every other word in the accent colour.
items.whenToUse: Rhythmic voice-overs, music-driven edits, meme pacing.
items.whenNotToUse: Brand voice that must look calm; mixed-colour words fight a busy, colourful plate.

items.name: One word, slam
items.summary: Condensed caps that slam in from oversize; key words punch in red.
items.whenToUse: Punchlines, reveals, sports and trailer-style hooks.
items.whenNotToUse: Every word of a long script; reserve the slam for emphasis beats.

items.name: One word, arcade
items.summary: 8-bit pixel type with a hard pixel shadow, one word per cut.
items.whenToUse: Gaming, scores, level-up moments, retro tech.
items.whenNotToUse: More than a few seconds of speech: pixel type is slow to read.

items.name: Three words, active highlight
items.summary: Three-word chunks pop in; the spoken word turns yellow.
items.whenToUse: The creator default: talking heads, explainers, podcasts clipped to shorts.
items.whenNotToUse: Luxury or editorial registers where caps and yellow read as cheap.

items.name: Three words, box highlight
items.summary: Sentence-case chunks slide up; a solid box sits behind the spoken word.
items.whenToUse: SaaS, tech and education; readable on any plate thanks to the box.
items.whenNotToUse: Very fast speech: the box jumping every 150 ms flickers.

items.name: Three words, underline
items.summary: Calm fade-in chunks; an accent underline draws under the spoken word.
items.whenToUse: Editorial, interviews, voice-over essays; emphasis without shouting.
items.whenNotToUse: Busy bright plates where a thin outline is not enough contrast (use the box or band).

items.name: Three words, handwritten note
items.summary: Handwritten words on a tilted paper note; the spoken word turns burnt orange.
items.whenToUse: UGC reviews, recipes, journaling, cosy and personal brands.
items.whenNotToUse: Corporate, technical or urgent content.

items.name: Three words, word reveal
items.summary: Each word rises into place as it is spoken; wide geometric type.
items.whenToUse: Product launches, fintech, modern brand voice.
items.whenNotToUse: Long words in narrow columns: the wide face needs short words.

items.name: Five words, karaoke fill
items.summary: Phrase-length chunks; spoken words fill with the accent colour and stay filled.
items.whenToUse: Storytelling, podcasts, longer voice-overs where one-word pacing would exhaust.
items.whenNotToUse: Hooks: five words at once are slower to land than one.

items.name: Five words, solid band
items.summary: Dark text on a white band that slides up; the spoken word turns red.
items.whenToUse: News, documentary, accessibility-first captions on any footage.
items.whenNotToUse: High-energy edits; a solid band feels static against fast cuts.

items.name: Five words, subtle
items.summary: Quiet sentence-case subtitles with a soft shadow; no highlight.
items.whenToUse: Premium, cinematic and documentary work where captions should disappear.
items.whenNotToUse: Bright plates without a dark area behind the text, and attention-hungry hooks.
